The main takeaway from our work is that
the L-band SAR backscatter–above ground biomass (AGBM) relationship is sensitive to the surface moisture conditions, which can be used to infer the moisture status of vegetation.
L-band backscattering intensifies when the soil and vegetation are wet, and this can affect the relationship between AGB and L-band backscattered intensities.
PALSAR backscatter can be used to estimate AGB of woodey vegetation, but the accuracy of these estimates is dependent on the moisture conditions and vegetation structures.
